author: Pedini
text:
Hey Hoto,

It really depends on my situation. Nearly always when I am at the charts
 I will watch for price action to add probability to a trade. Once you
learn to do this, you will keep yourself out of a lot of bad ones. Even
the trades I am not around for, PA was the reason I would have set a PO.
 I trade mainly after I see an engulf of an important swing, to me, this
 is PA. If price is reaching an important level, but forms a base just
before it reaches it, this is PA and may stop me from entering. So
again, pretty much all my trades are PA related.

Ped

I don't mean the PA that is in the past. I am talking about the trades
you are taking when price returns to a current zone. Sometimes it looks
like you are taking trades when price returns to a zone without watching
 PA. Other times you don't enter until price enters the zone and PA
approves. I understand that current PA is higher probability, but how do
 you know when to enter?

Look at your charts in post 80 and 86. The last chart in post 80 showed
you entering when price returned to that level after the FO. Post 86 you
 entered at the FTR without PA when price returned to it. It seems that
you just entered a PO at that FTR level.

Hopefully this question makes sense.

Thanks,

H

author: Pedini
text:
Hey Hoto,

I see where you are going with this, but I have to be honest and don't
exactly know how to answer your question. I will normally be comfortable
 touch trading a bread and butter setup after and engulf of a important
level, but If i am at the computer screen I will also watch PA.
Sometimes I do it, sometimes I don't, but I always wait for an engulf
before I enter. I suppose the more confident I am with a level the more
likely I am to touch trade. Sometimes the markets just call for some
extra conformation from me.

L

I hope I am not a pest to you. I am just trying to sort all of this out.
 Its hard with so many people that call things by different names and
trade a little differently. So the main point for me to start with is
that we are looking for an engulf (which is also ignored demand/supply)
on a key level, right? Then you watch for a FTR or touch trade of that
level, right? When you are touch trading are you just going down to
lower time frames to find a FTR?

Thanks for all your help Pedini! Again, I hope I am not being a pest to you.

Thanks,

H

author: Pedini
text:
No not at all Hoto,

This is exactly why this community is around :)

Pretty much spot on. Mark out your higher S/D levels. Look for an engulf
 of important levels. Find the source of the move. These are to me high
probability trades and these types of trades are very very good RR and
even if they aren't all correct, you will end up well in profit for the
ones that are.

L

out and won't be back till monday. But here is a perfect example of an

See when I read your stuff it makes perfect sense. I can see what
exactly you did and why. The only thing left off of the chart was the
location of the cap. I am going to assume that the cap was on/around a
key level in the higher time frame. I think this is going on right now
in the AUD/USD. So your key here is that price capped so nicely, thats
why you are touch trading, right? Otherwise you would have to wait for
price to come back to the location that you entered at as a FTR, right? I
 say this because price engulfed, returned to the cap and then made a
new low, thats what makes it a correct FTR, right?

Enjoy your vacation. Australia has always been a life dream of mine
making it there. Don't know what I am going to do on a plane for 18
hours, but I would do it.

Thanks,

Once you get some more screen time looking in the right direction, these
 opportunities will become obvious. The cap is pretty obvious in the
chart I have posted. It is exactly where I entered. If has a great video
 on caps which im sure you have seen which explains them nicely. Key is I
 am happy to take a TT if a good setup shows...if I TT 10 identical
setups after seeing an engulf of an important level, I am confident I
was be in positive pipage, it is very important if you have a system,
that you stay consistent.

text:
Me and Sunny were in this one together. I thought I would post a
little big more about our TG. Firstly, our tg was higher at supply. But

Always remember, if your price situations change, so do your trades.
